हमारा देश भारत गाँवों का देश है। यहाँ की अधिकांश जनसंख्या गाँवों में ही निवास करती है। भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था के विकास में कुटीर उद्योग, पशुधन, वन-संपदा तथा मौसमी फल और सब्जियों के योगदान की अनदेखी नहीं की जा सकती। वर्तमान समय में भी गाँव देश की अर्थव्यवस्था में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभा रहे हैं। वास्तव में हमारे देश की आत्मा गाँवों में ही बसती है। इन गाँवों में मेहनतकश किसान और मजदूर कार्य करते हैं, जो देश के अन्नदाता हैं। किसानों के परिश्रम से हमें खाद्यान्न प्राप्त होता है और वे भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था को सुदृढ़ बनाने में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान देते हैं। देश की समृद्धि किसानों के श्रम और त्याग पर ही निर्भर करती है।यदि देश का वास्तविक स्वरूप देखना हो तो वह गाँवों में ही दृष्टिगोचर होता है। गाँव हमारी सभ्यता और संस्कृति के प्रतीक हैं। स्वतंत्रता प्राप्ति से पूर्व यदि गाँवों के विकास पर पर्याप्त ध्यान दिया गया होता, तो आज उनकी स्थिति और भी बेहतर होती। आदिम मानव प्रारंभ में जंगलों और गुफाओं में निवास करता था। जैसे-जैसे उसने प्रगति की, वैसे-वैसे गाँवों का स्वरूप विकसित हुआ। यहीं से ग्राम्य सभ्यता का उद्भव हुआ और आगे चलकर नगर सभ्यता की नींव पड़ी। आज भी शहरों की अपेक्षा गाँवों में प्राकृतिक सौंदर्य अधिक है। वहाँ प्रकृति अपने स्वाभाविक और निर्मल रूप में विद्यमान है, जिसमें कृत्रिमता का अभाव है। इस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है कि शहरों के जन्मदाता भी गाँव ही हैं।

Pierre, unexpectedly enriched through inheritance, searches for moral and intellectual purpose, confronting existential uncertainty and the burden of privilege. Prince Andrei, disillusioned with aristocratic triviality, seeks glory in battle only to confront the futility and devastation of war. Natasha’s emotional evolution, shaped by love and heartbreak, becomes a vital representation of resilience and youthful vulnerability.

Tolstoy juxtaposes tranquil aristocratic life with the brutality of warfare, presenting the Battle of Borodino and its aftermath as emblematic of collective suffering. Through shifting perspectives, he reveals how conflict reshapes families, ambitions, and loyalties, exposing the fragility of human aspirations. The narrative is punctuated by philosophical reflections on history and agency, challenging the idea that great individuals determine historical outcomes. Instead, Tolstoy attributes societal transformation to countless ordinary decisions, coincidences, and material conditions that transcend personal will.

Set against aristocratic salons and rural estates, the story interrogates social performance, spiritual longing, and the tension between personal desire and historical necessity. Pierre’s eventual enlightenment contrasts with Andrei’s disenchanted withdrawal, illustrating divergent responses to existential upheaval. Natasha’s capacity for emotional renewal suggests that compassion and connection endure even as empires collapse. By the novel’s conclusion, hopes for peace coexist with the enduring scars of conflict, reinforcing Tolstoy’s belief that history is lived not only through battles and politics but also through private suffering and moral awakening. Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Ultra-processed foods require more precise classification, argues a 03 September 2025 editorial in Nature, as the United Nations General Assembly prepares to debate eliminating trans fatty acids from diets worldwide. These fats, predominantly industrial in origin, heighten cardiovascular risk, prompting more than sixty countries to restrict them and nine to fully remove them from food supplies. Public health researchers caution, however, that UN wording must specify “industrially produced” trans fats to avoid discouraging consumption of nutrient-essential natural trans fats in dairy, especially in low-income regions where caloric adequacy remains fragile. This concern feeds into a wider scientific dispute over the definition and regulatory impact of ultra-processed foods. The influential NOVA classification, introduced in 2009 by Carlos Monteiro, categorises foods by the extent and purpose of processing. Items composed largely of industrial extracts and additives fall into the ultra-processed tier and have been linked to obesity and cardiovascular disease, motivating strong policy responses in Latin America, including taxes and mandatory front-of-pack warnings.

Yet critics argue that processing alone cannot determine nutritional harm. Palatability, craving-inducing additives and high energy density significantly influence dietary behaviour. Moreover, NOVA’s broad categories conflate heterogeneous products: baby formula, sliced bread and chicken nuggets are all labelled ultra-processed despite distinct processing rationales and social functions. Even the system’s proponents acknowledge that many forms of processing, such as pasteurisation or freezing, provide clear public health benefits. Governments and research bodies now seek refined terminology that limits harmful industrial excess while safeguarding access to adequate nutrition. With obesity and undernutrition coexisting globally, policy cannot rely on vague classifications but must balance dietary risk reduction with food security.
